name: wrapped-argument-list
note: layout only

name: wrapped-argument-list-trailing-comma
note: a trailing comma is a token

name: return-then-line-break
note: same tokens, different tree: the return now returns nothing

name: reindented-template
note: whitespace inside a template is content
head:
const s = `line one
      line two`;

name: reindented-block
note: indentation outside any literal

name: blank-lines-between-statements
note: blank lines only
head:
const a = 1;


const b = 2;

name: comment-added
note: a prose comment of several words is no token and no directive

name: comment-marker-inside-string
note: // inside a string is content, not a comment
head: const u = "http://a // b";

name: postfix-increment-line-break
note: same tokens, different tree: ++ now belongs to the next statement

name: arrow-body-wrapped
note: layout only
head:
const f = (x: number) =>
  x * 2;

name: jsx-text-reflowed
note: JSX text is content
head:
const e =

one two

;

name: jsx-attributes-wrapped
note: layout between attributes
head:
const e = <a
    href="x"
    title="y"
  />;

name: quote-style
note: a string's spelling is its token text
head: const s = "a";

name: semicolon-added
note: a semicolon is a token
head: const a = 1;

name: json-reindented
note: JSON layout

name: json-key-order
note: key order is a change
head: {"b":2,"a":1}

name: comment-bare-word-added
note: no token changes, but a single bare word is flagged a directive by the engine, so the extended rule reads a change

name: directive-comment-changed
base:
// @ts-expect-error old reason
const a: number = f();
head:
// @ts-expect-error new reason
const a: number = f();
note: a comment a tool obeys changed

name: trailing-whitespace-removed
head:
const a = 1;
const b = 2;
note: the gap after the semicolon holds a line break on both sides

name: aligned-with-spaces
head:
const a  = 1;
const bb = 2;
note: whitespace on one line on both sides, spaces only

name: tab-replaces-spaces
note: a gap holding a tab must be byte-identical

name: blank-line-added-in-argument-list
note: a line break was already there

name: line-comment-forces-a-break
head:
const s = a + // Sum of the two parts.
  b;
note: the comment is prose of several words, but the gap between + and b gains a line break

name: go-generate-indented
note: go generate runs the first and ignores the second: the whitespace before a flagged comment must be byte-identical (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: go-line-directive-indented
note: the //line form must start at the beginning of a line (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: cgo-preamble-blank-line
note: cgo uses the preamble only when it immediately precedes the import: the whitespace after a flagged comment must be byte-identical (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: cgo-preamble-prose-blank-line
note: the preamble reads as prose and is flagged by position only: flagged at the base, not at the head, so the flagged comments differ in number (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: python-coding-cookie-pushed
head:
# -*- coding: latin-1 -*-
x = 1
note: the declaration counts only on line 1 or 2 (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: python-tab-for-spaces
note: TabError at run time; the tree counts a tab as eight columns: a gap holding a tab must be byte-identical (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: shebang-after-space
head:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
x = 1
note: the file stops being an executable script (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: ts-abstract-line-break
head:
abstract
class A {}
note: tsc parses an expression statement and a class that is no longer abstract: an inline gap became a line break (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: ts-export-default-abstract-line-break
head:
export default abstract
class A {}
note: tsc parses the head differently (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: ts-using-line-break
note: tsc parses the head differently (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: ts-interface-line-break
head:
interface
I {}
note: tsc parses the head differently (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: js-async-arrow-line-break
head:
const f = async
(x) => x;
note: V8 raises a SyntaxError (from the graph lane's engine review; equal leaves on both sides, so only the gap rule or the directive conditions see it)

name: ts-line-break-inside-block-comment
base: function f() { return /* see the note below */ 1; }
head:
function f() { return /* see the note
 below */ 1; }
note: tsc ends the return at a line break inside a comment, so it loses its value; the leaves are equal and the comment is prose: the stretch between return and 1 gains a line feed inside the comment's own bytes (from the graph lane's engine review)

name: go-line-break-inside-block-comment
base:
package a

func f() int { return /* see the note below */ 1 }
note: Go inserts a semicolon at the line break inside the comment, so the head does not compile (from the graph lane's engine review)
